title: 1 Parking Poste de Secours, 19380 Albussac, France - Albussac grande cascade_
author: kaoss012
notes: Albussac 'grande cascade' (Correze, France), natural forest waterfall roar, Zoom H6, lossless 44.1k stereo. Rock-steady texture (LRA 0.7), dense low-mid roar with natural top to ~10 kHz, no voices/traffic/birds visible. Segment skips the recordist's fade-in (first ~14 s) and fade-out (last ~7 s).

title: QJCC+35 Saint-Mamet, France - Cascade de Sidonie
author: kaoss012
notes: Cascade de Sidonie near Luchon (Pyrenees, France), same recordist/kit (Zoom H6), lossless. Brighter, more open roar than Albussac; mid band level constant to +/-0.5 dB over the whole segment, LF (20-80 Hz) steady at ~-40 dB (falls rumble, not wind gusts). Fade-in/out excluded. Pair with falls-1 for variety.

title: Derrysallagh, Geevagh, Co. Sligo, Ireland - Babbling Stream
author: Benjamin Burns
notes: Babbling stream (Derrysallagh, Co. Sligo, Ireland), Zoom H1 held just above the water surface on a calm sunny day; lossless 44.1k. Very consistent close-up babble/trickle texture (LRA 0.7), energy 250 Hz-8 kHz, nothing below ~200 Hz (no wind rumble), no voices/vehicles. Caveat: H1 XY is fairly narrow (L/R corr 0.84) and the texture is even rather than 'gurgle-event' rich.

title: Unnamed Road, 76596 Forbach, Deutschland - Rote Lache - Black Forest, morning birds
author: avoelzing
notes: Rote Lache, Black Forest (Germany): forest morning ambience with several songbirds at medium/far distance, no water. Lossless 48k stereo. Traffic band (150-1000 Hz) is flat - no vehicle or aircraft swells; birdsong 2-9 kHz throughout. Caveats: quiet recording (-37 LUFS) with a steady sub-100 Hz rumble (wind/air) - a high-pass around 80-100 Hz is recommended; birds are fairly busy (spring morning)

title: Sherwood Forest - Wind in the Trees
author: rcarlberg
notes: Wind high in the tree canopy ('wash of white noise') on a clear day, gentle-to-moderate gusts swelling every 20-40 s, energy 250 Hz-3 kHz, no mic-wind rumble blobs in this segment (the two small LF bumps at 84 s and 228 s are excluded). Source is a 69-min 320 kbps MP3; the local file is the first 300 s of it (byte-range download), times are identical to the original. Faint insect ticks 3-5 kHz. Ca

title: East Hampton Waterfall
author: paperhurts
license: recorded for Ambiance, used with permission
notes: Recorded on a phone by the app's owner at the waterfall she drove her son to so he'd fall asleep, 31 Dec 2019, specifically as background sound. Steady (LRA 0.2 LU), no voices, handling or clipping; first and last moments of the clip left out.

title: XC692210 Wood Thrush
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: One complete song: soft low intro notes, the flute phrase (a held 4.6 kHz note sliding down to 2.9 kHz, then a 4-pulse 'ee-oh-lay' ladder at 3.3-3.9 kHz) and a rattling trill ending (9.6->5.2 kHz), with a 0.3 s decay tail. In-band SNR ~44 dB (hp 1500). Recorded at Cow Path Lane, Hollis, Hillsborough Co., New Hampshire, 2021-05-19. Source: mono 48 kHz MP3 ~94k; recordist already high-passed below ~

title: XC692210 Wood Thrush
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: One complete song of a different type from the same bird: intro notes, a buzzy 3.6 kHz figure plus two up-slurred flute notes (3.0->4.0 kHz), then a dense high trill (6.2-10 kHz). In-band SNR ~51 dB (hp 1500). Recorded at Cow Path Lane, Hollis, Hillsborough Co., New Hampshire, 2021-05-19. Source: mono 48 kHz MP3 ~94k; recordist already high-passed below ~2.5 kHz.

title: XC724428 Wood Thrush
author: Jorge de Leon Cardozo & Susan Hochgraf
notes: One complete song from the Connecticut bird: a held 4.6 kHz note sliding to 2.9 kHz, a ladder 'ee-oh-lay' at 3.3-3.9 kHz and a long, very regular trill (7-10 kHz). The start is set after an unrelated quick call at 21.1 s. In-band SNR ~37 dB (hp 1500). Recorded at 721 Middle Turnpike, Mansfield, Tolland Co., Connecticut, 2022-05-15. Source: stereo 48 kHz MP3 128k, but the right channel is ~30 dB do

title: XC724428 Wood Thrush
author: Jorge de Leon Cardozo & Susan Hochgraf
notes: One complete song from the Connecticut bird: low 'bup-bup-bup' intro notes (2.9 kHz), a 5.4->3.8 kHz slide plus a warbled 3.9-4.4 kHz figure, and a down-slurred trill (9.6->7 kHz). The floor at 1.5-2.5 kHz is a little higher here (road/stream noise ~45 dB below the song). In-band SNR ~39 dB (hp 1500). Recorded at 721 Middle Turnpike, Mansfield, Tolland Co., Connecticut, 2022-05-15. Source: stereo

title: XC692192 Veery
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: One complete song: the up-slurred 'vee' intro (3.5->5 kHz), then the descending, spiralling 'veer-veer-veer' series (6.2 down to 2.9 kHz), with a clean tail. In-band SNR ~51 dB (hp 1500). Recorded at Cow Path Lane, Hollis, Hillsborough Co., New Hampshire, 2021-05-17. Source: mono 48 kHz MP3 ~93k, recordist-filtered lows.

title: XC692192 Veery
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: One complete song, the same type as veery-1 with slightly different spirals (louder take): up-slur intro, then 4 descending spiral phrases. In-band SNR ~52 dB (hp 1500). Recorded at Cow Path Lane, Hollis, Hillsborough Co., New Hampshire, 2021-05-17. Source: mono 48 kHz MP3 ~93k, recordist-filtered lows.

title: XC602569 Veery
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: One complete song from a second individual: a high-starting type (spirals beginning around 6.2 kHz) with 4 descending, ringing phrases down to ~3.3 kHz. In-band SNR ~47 dB (hp 1500). Recorded at Lancy Brook Wetlands, Brookline/Mason, Hillsborough Co., New Hampshire, 2020-06-03. Source: mono 48 kHz MP3 192k; busy wetland chorus behind, other birds 30-45 dB down.

title: XC602569 Veery
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: One complete long song from the second individual: up-slur intro and 6 evenly spaced spiral phrases (5.5-3.4 kHz). A very faint 5.8 kHz whistle from another bird ~45 dB down; another species starts after 88.95 s and is excluded. In-band SNR ~42 dB (hp 1500). title: XC691611 Louisiana Waterthrush
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: One complete song: 4 ringing, down-slurred 'seeup' notes (8->5.8 kHz), then the jumbled, sputtering twitter (7->3.5 kHz). In-band SNR ~46 dB (hp 2000). Recorded at Cow Path Lane, Hollis, Hillsborough Co., New Hampshire, 2021-05-21. Source: mono 48 kHz MP3 ~93k, recordist-filtered lows.

title: XC175483 Louisiana Waterthrush
author: Peter Wilton
notes: One complete song from a second individual (Massachusetts): one short and 2 long slurred notes from 8 kHz, then the twitter of V-shaped notes and fast sweeps. In-band SNR ~50 dB (hp 2000). Recorded at Carlisle, Middlesex Co., Massachusetts, 2014-04-21. Source: stereo 44.1 kHz MP3 256k (LR corr 0.76); a steady ~1 kHz band at about -50 dB (stream?) sits far below the hp.

title: XC415057 Louisiana Waterthrush
author: John Baur
notes: One complete song from a third, more distant individual: 3 long slurred notes from 8.6 kHz, with audible ravine reverb smearing each note, then a softer twitter (7-4.5 kHz). The level is lower (in-band peak -25 dB), so normalise it. In-band SNR ~30 dB (hp 2500). Recorded at Clinton (near Lancaster), Worcester Co., Massachusetts, 2018-05-06. Source: stereo 44.1 kHz MP3 176k; more distant bird with

title: XC175483 Louisiana Waterthrush
author: Peter Wilton
notes: A second song from the Massachusetts bird, with an extra closing note (7.3 kHz) after the twitter. In-band SNR ~50 dB (hp 2000). Recorded at Carlisle, Middlesex Co., Massachusetts, 2014-04-21. Source: stereo 44.1 kHz MP3 256k (LR corr 0.76); a steady ~1 kHz band at about -50 dB (stream?) sits far below the hp.

title: XC692204 Winter Wren
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: One complete 5 s song (type 1): soft opening notes, rapid 5 kHz trills, cascading warbles and a high 8.6 kHz trill finish. At the very end a faint, distant bird is about 50 dB down. In-band SNR ~47 dB (hp 2500). Recorded at Cow Path Lane, Hollis, Hillsborough Co., New Hampshire, 2021-05-03. Source: mono 48 kHz MP3 ~95k, recordist-filtered lows; faint distant birds 45+ dB down.

title: XC692204 Winter Wren
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: One complete song of a second type from the same bird: it opens with a fast 10-note 5 kHz ladder, then warbles and a high trill ending (8.6 kHz). Faint low tonal dashes at 0.7 and 1.4 kHz near the end sit below the hp. In-band SNR ~46 dB (hp 2500). Recorded at Cow Path Lane, Hollis, Hillsborough Co., New Hampshire, 2021-05-03. Source: mono 48 kHz MP3 ~95k, recordist-filtered lows; faint distant bi

title: XC602670 Winter Wren
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: One complete 5.7 s song from a second individual (Massachusetts): soft intro notes, then a long bubbling cascade with a 4.8 kHz trill, many rising and falling sweeps up to 9 kHz and a descending 9->8 kHz flourish at the end. A distant second wren is faintly audible (~25-30 dB down) at the start. In-band SNR ~48 dB (hp 2500). Recorded at Skinner State Park (near Hadley), Hampshire Co., Massachusett

title: XC819318 Winter Wren
author: Trent R. Stanley
notes: One complete song from a third individual (Vermont): a jumble of trills (4.8-7.5 kHz) ending in a long, shimmering 8.6 kHz trill. The perspective is slightly more distant, from a lossless source. In-band SNR ~41 dB (hp 2500). Recorded at Centennial Woods Natural Area (near Burlington), Chittenden Co., Vermont, 2023-07-17. Source: lossless 24-bit 192 kHz stereo WAV (saved as XC819318.mp3 per the na

title: XC375275 Red-eyed Vireo
author: Susan Hochgraf
notes: Recorded: Bigelow Hollow State Park (Breakneck Pond), Union, Connecticut, 2017-05-27 10:30; singing from hemlock-hardwood understory ~20 m away. One phrase: low wavering notes then a sharp up-slur to ~4.5 kHz ('here I am?'), with the forest's natural reverb tail (~0.4 s). In-band SNR ~37 dB. Left channel is near-silent in the bird band (bird is in R only), so the mono downmix is clean, just 6 dB l

title: XC375275 Red-eyed Vireo
author: Susan Hochgraf
notes: Recorded: Bigelow Hollow State Park (Breakneck Pond), Union, Connecticut, 2017-05-27 10:30; singing from hemlock-hardwood understory ~20 m away. One phrase: a rapid ascending wavy series (~3-4.5 kHz) followed by two lower notes; long reverberant decay kept. Same bird as -1, different phrase shape. In-band SNR ~38 dB.

title: XC802222 Red-eyed Vireo
author: Jim Berry
notes: Recorded: Carroll (near Frewsburg), Chautauqua Co., New York, 2023-05-14 08:30; mixed hemlock/deciduous forest with a stream (stream wash 200-1800 Hz under the bird, removed by hp). One phrase: three-part descending phrase starting high (~6 kHz) and stepping down to a wiggle at ~2.5 kHz. Mono-compatible (L=R). In-band SNR ~32 dB; very faint other-bird whistle (~-50 dB) just before the onset.

title: XC802222 Red-eyed Vireo
author: Jim Berry
notes: Recorded: Carroll (near Frewsburg), Chautauqua Co., New York, 2023-05-14 08:30; mixed hemlock/deciduous forest with a stream (stream wash 200-1800 Hz under the bird, removed by hp). One phrase: down-slur into a wavering 'where are you' wiggle (~2.5-4.5 kHz). Same NY bird as -3. In-band SNR ~33 dB.

title: XC421274 Eastern Wood Pewee
author: GABRIEL LEITE
notes: Recorded: Caroline (near Brooktondale), Tompkins Co., New York, 2018-06-17 07:30. One slow 'pee-a-wee': rising-dipping onset then a long held note (~3.2-4 kHz), tail kept. In-band SNR ~30 dB. Strong low-frequency background in the file (removed by hp); a faint other-bird band at ~4.5-5 kHz sits well under the bird.

title: XC421274 Eastern Wood Pewee
author: GABRIEL LEITE
notes: Recorded: Caroline (near Brooktondale), Tompkins Co., New York, 2018-06-17 07:30. One 'pee-ur': rises to ~3.8 kHz then slurs slowly down to ~3 kHz. In-band SNR ~28 dB. The note stops cleanly at 28.12 (little natural reverb here) and a twig-like click follows at 28.24, so the clip ends at 28.22 with a short 0.1 s fade_out so the note isn't faded away.

title: XC1014872 Eastern Wood Pewee
author: Stanislas Wroza
notes: Recorded: Marais Leon-Provancher, Portneuf, Quebec (widened region; WAV 48 kHz). One classic 'pee-a-wee' (quick rise to 4.2 kHz, dip, slow rise to ~3.9 kHz), very clean: in-band SNR ~55 dB, quiet marsh-edge background. Stereo channels well correlated in band (0.85), safe to downmix.

title: XC1014872 Eastern Wood Pewee
author: Stanislas Wroza
notes: Recorded: Marais Leon-Provancher, Portneuf, Quebec (widened region; WAV 48 kHz). One down-slurred 'pee-ur' (high onset ~5 kHz, sliding down to ~2.6 kHz over ~1 s). Same Quebec bird as -3. In-band SNR ~50 dB. Band L/R correlation 0.46: mono mix measured only 1-4 dB under the louder channel, no deep phase notches.

title: XC598808 Black-capped Chickadee
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: Recorded: Brookline, Hillsborough Co., New Hampshire, 2019-06-22 15:00. One whistled 'fee-bee' song (fee ~4 kHz, bee ~3.5 kHz) with reverb tail. In-band SNR ~50 dB. A distant second chickadee answers ~30 dB down between songs (outside the cut). Mono-compatible.

title: XC598808 Black-capped Chickadee
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: Recorded: Brookline, Hillsborough Co., New Hampshire, 2019-06-22 15:00. Another 'fee-bee' from the same NH bird (slightly different timing/pitch), clean gaps either side, tail kept. In-band SNR ~50 dB.

title: XC134017 Black-capped Chickadee
author: Dan Lane
notes: Recorded: Manomet Bird Observatory, Plymouth Co., Massachusetts, 1994-02-04; coastal second growth. One 'chick-a-dee-dee-dee' call: 6 high 'chick-a' notes (6-8 kHz) then 6 buzzy 'dee' notes (harmonics 1.6-5 kHz). Mono, quiet background (recordist high-passed ~450 Hz). In-band SNR ~34 dB. Winter recording, coastal woodland.

title: XC134017 Black-capped Chickadee
author: Dan Lane
notes: Recorded: Manomet Bird Observatory, Plymouth Co., Massachusetts, 1994-02-04; coastal second growth. Shorter 'chick-a-dee-dee' call: 6 'chick' notes then 3 'dee' notes. Same MA bird as -3. In-band SNR ~34 dB.

title: XC381798 White-breasted Nuthatch
author: Sue Riffe
notes: Recorded: Ross Rd (near Orchard Beach), York Co., Maine, 2017-06-07 13:50; recordist notes car traffic in the background (below ~1 kHz, removed by hp). One 'wer-wer-wer' song (series of ~9 nasal notes, 1.3-2.5 kHz). Mono. In-band SNR ~30 dB; recordist notes car traffic, which is below ~1 kHz and goes with the hp. Faint other-bird whistle at 4-5 kHz before the song, ~25 dB down.

title: XC233937 White-breasted Nuthatch
author: Albert Lastukhin & Max Lastukhin
notes: Recorded: Oyster Bay (near Lattingtown), Nassau Co., New York, 2015-03-12 07:30; S. c. carolinensis; heavy low-frequency background (surf/traffic) below 1 kHz, removed by hp. One fast 'wer-wer-wer' song (~19 notes over 2.3 s at ~2.2 kHz with harmonics 1.4/3 kHz), eastern subspecies S. c. carolinensis. In-band SNR ~33 dB. Strong low-frequency background (<1 kHz) removed by hp; faint House Sparrow c

title: XC837636 White-breasted Nuthatch
author: Valerie Heemstra
notes: Recorded: Ford River Township (near Escanaba), Delta Co., Michigan, 2023-10-23 09:30; single bird foraging (widened region); strong wind rumble <100 Hz and wash up to ~1 kHz, removed by hp. One series of ~12 nasal 'yank' calls (harmonic stacks 1.05-3.5 kHz), single foraging bird. In-band SNR ~27 dB. Lake-shore wind: big rumble <100 Hz and a wash up to ~1 kHz, needs the hp; a faint residual wash wi

title: XC1034477 American Crow
author: Rory Nefdt
notes: American crow, 5 quick caws in one series with a short natural woods reverb tail. Pound Ridge Reservation, Lewisboro, Westchester Co., New York (2025-08-31, 17:30, Olympus L-14). Mid-distance bird (fundamental ~1.3 kHz, weak upper harmonics), about +26 dB over the floor in its band. A steady late-summer katydid band at 5-8 kHz sits under the whole file; lp 4500 removes it.

title: XC1034477 American Crow
author: Rory Nefdt
notes: American crow, 5-caw series from the same bird as american-crow-1 (Pound Ridge Reservation, Westchester Co., NY), about +27 dB in band, clean gaps on both sides. The lp 4500 is for the katydid band at 5-8 kHz.

title: XC1034477 American Crow
author: Rory Nefdt
notes: American crow, short 3-caw series from the same bird (Pound Ridge Reservation, Westchester Co., NY), about +25 dB in band. Gives a shorter variation. The lp 4500 is for the katydid band.

title: XC460987 American Crow
author: Meena Haribal
notes: American crow, 4 caws from a mid-distance bird with a natural reverb tail. DeRuyter (near Georgetown), Madison Co., New York (2019-03-09, 08:30, stereo 192k). Very quiet floor (about +38 dB in band). A different individual and timbre from clips 1-3. Faint evening grosbeak chirps around 3.5 kHz near the end are about 35 dB below the caws.

title: XC460987 American Crow
author: Meena Haribal
notes: American crow, 4 caws from the same DeRuyter, NY bird as american-crow-4, about +36 dB in band, long natural decay tail. A faint evening grosbeak chatter (~3.5 kHz) is low in the background.

title: XC599832 Pileated Woodpecker
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: Species: Pileated woodpecker (Dryocopus pileatus). One drum roll of about 1.6 s (~22 strikes, ~14/s) that trails off in level and decays naturally; resonant body at 340-450 Hz. HBHS, Hollis, Hillsborough Co., New Hampshire (2019-04-03). Near-silent floor, about +40 dB in band.

title: XC599832 Pileated Woodpecker
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: Species: Pileated woodpecker (Dryocopus pileatus). A second drum roll (~1.6 s) from the same Hollis, NH bird as woodpecker-1, with a slow trailing finish and about 0.5 s of decay. About +39 dB over a very quiet floor.

title: XC915954 Pileated Woodpecker
author: Meena Haribal
notes: Species: Pileated woodpecker (Dryocopus pileatus). A long (~2.3 s), loud, resonant roll at 250-700 Hz from a different bird: Piercefield (near Childwold), St. Lawrence Co., New York, Adirondacks (2024-06-06; recordist: 'slow rhythmic drumming, it was heavenly'). Lossless 24-bit WAV source (saved as .mp3 name). The bird is close. The file has wind rumble below 100 Hz and a steady noise band below ~

title: XC915954 Pileated Woodpecker
author: Meena Haribal
notes: Species: Pileated woodpecker (Dryocopus pileatus). A classic 'wuk-wuk-wuk' laughing call series (~22 notes over 2.8 s, bands at 1 and 2 kHz) with a natural tail. Same Adirondack, NY recording (lossless) as woodpecker-3. About +47 dB in band above the floor; hp 700 removes the low wind and water noise completely.

title: XC797066 Pileated Woodpecker
author: Jim Berry
notes: Species: Pileated woodpecker (Dryocopus pileatus). A 'wuk-wuk' call series (~13 notes, 1.7 s) from a different bird: Busti (near Jamestown), Chautauqua Co., New York (2023-04-30, 06:30). The recordist applied light noise reduction and a 250 Hz high-pass. About +44 dB in band. There is some extra curved 1-1.6 kHz energy under the notes, possibly a second pileated or another bird, and a faint 2.3 kH

title: XC599324 Downy Woodpecker
author: Christopher McPherson
notes: Species: Downy woodpecker (Dryobates pubescens). One short, even drum roll (~1.3 s, ~17 strikes/s, tonal ~900 Hz) with a natural decay. Mine Falls, Nashua, Hillsborough Co., New Hampshire (2019-04-29). About +31 dB in band. Faint songbird chips at 3-6 kHz in the background are about 30 dB down.
